articles.title: September GST: gross ₹2.04 lakh crore (+14.7%), and imports, not domestic demand, are carrying the growth — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The headline is strong, but the composition is the exam point. Import-linked GST is growing about 2.5 times as fast as domestic GST, which is a ready Mains line on the quality of tax buoyancy. It also gives you a data set to quote for GS3 on revenue mobilisation.
**Memorise:** Released **1 Oct 2026** (provisional). **Gross GST ₹2.04 lakh crore** (+**14.7%** from ₹1.77 lakh crore in Sept 2025). **Net GST ₹1.77 lakh crore** (+**18.1%**). **Domestic ₹1.38 lakh crore** (+10.1%); **import-linked ₹65,525 crore** (+25.9%). **Refunds ₹27,001 crore** (−3%). **April–Sept FY27 gross: ₹12.46 lakh crore** (+11.6%); over the half-year, import GST is up **27.1%** against **6.1%** for domestic. State-wise: **Maharashtra ₹29,986 crore** (+15%) leads, **Karnataka ₹13,884 crore** (+16%), **Assam +88%** is the fastest riser. *Mains line:* "A tax base that grows on imports is only as durable as the import bill."
**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (Public finance; Taxation).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Economy, *Taxation → GST (structure, IGST, GST Council, compensation)*; Laxmikanth, *Art. 246A, Art. 279A*. *Nudge:* add a "gross vs net vs domestic vs import" row for Sept 2026 to your monthly GST tracker, and cross-link to your note on the Union–State fiscal federalism angle.

articles.title: Goyal at the US-hosted G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee — India pushes for an interim trade deal alongside — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The US holds the 2026 G20 presidency, so India's trade diplomacy and the G20 track meet in one visit. For Prelims, the testable layer is how the G20 works (troika, no secretariat, membership). For Mains, it illustrates India's "bilateral plus multilateral" trade strategy while talks with Washington continue.
**Memorise:** Commerce Minister **Piyush Goyal** is in the US from **29 Sept to 5 Oct 2026** (Milwaukee, with Chicago and New York legs) for the **G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting**. The **US holds the 2026 G20 presidency**. In Milwaukee he joined a **National Association of Manufacturers (NAM)** business roundtable (US manufacturing GDP about **$3 trillion**) and a Business Roundtable–NAM reception, and pitched India as an investment destination. Media reports frame the visit as a push for an **interim India–US trade deal**; those talks have been described as dragging, and no deal had been announced at the time of writing *(treat the deal status as fluid)*.
**Notebook:** GS2 – IR (Bilateral and multilateral groupings; India–USA); GS3 – Economy (External sector).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / IR notes, *Global groupings → G20* (members, troika, working tracks: Finance and Sherpa). *Nudge:* add "2026 presidency: USA" to your G20 chair timeline and cross-link to your India–USA trade note and the India–New Zealand FTA entry (26 Sept).

articles.title: ISRO lines up seven launches by March 2027, and the second spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam is due in 2026-27 — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The launch pipeline ties together the Gaganyaan programme, the small-launcher segment and India's launch-site geography. The Kulasekarapattinam spaceport is a likely "Places in News" and static-science hybrid. The SSLV hand-over to a private manufacturer is a good example of the Indian Space Policy 2023 in action.
**Memorise:** ISRO Chairman **V. Narayanan** said **seven launches** are planned by **March 2027** using **PSLV, GSLV, LVM3 and SSLV**; missions include the first **uncrewed Gaganyaan** flight plus Earth-observation, communication and navigation satellites. He said **two satellites are ready** and **five to six missions** are in final integration. The second spaceport at **Kulasekarapattinam (Tamil Nadu)** is expected to become operational in **2026-27** for **SSLV** launches. Background: the **SSLV technology** was transferred to **HAL**, which won manufacturing rights after a competition; **IN-SPACe** authorises private space activity and **NSIL** handles commercial deals. *(One report's vehicle-wise counts did not add up to seven, so only the total and vehicle list are used here.)*
**Notebook:** GS3 – Science & Technology (Space).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / Shankar IAS, *Space technology → launch vehicles (PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV) and launch sites*. *Nudge:* add a "Sriharikota (AP) vs Kulasekarapattinam (TN)" row to your launch-site table, with SSLV against polar and geosynchronous orbits, and cross-link to your IN-SPACe / Space Policy 2023 note.

articles.title: CAQM rewrites GRAP before winter: diesel generators and bus curbs move into Stage I, and construction oversight widens — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The shift is from reacting to a smog episode to front-loading curbs. It tests your grasp of GRAP as a *graded, AQI-triggered* tool run by a statutory commission, which is the core of the Delhi air-pollution case study for Mains.
**Memorise:** Approved by the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** on **28 Sept 2026**. **Diesel generator-set** and **inter-city bus** restrictions moved from **Stage II to Stage I**. **Stage III** limits on **BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel** vehicles now extend to **Sonipat** and border areas of **Ghaziabad, Faridabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar**. Directions **11–18** extend construction oversight beyond municipal limits (controlled areas, industrial areas, highway corridors); projects of **500 sq m and above** must register on the state pollution board portal and install monitoring cameras. The **Citizen Charter** grows from **22 to 34 actions**. Separately, Delhi announced a **construction ban from 1 Nov**. CAQM is a statutory body under the **CAQM Act, 2021**. Standard GRAP stages by AQI: **I Poor (201–300), II Very Poor (301–400), III Severe (401–450), IV Severe+ (>450)**.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (Pollution; institutions).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, *Environmental Pollution → Air pollution (NCAP, AQI, GRAP, CAQM)*. *Nudge:* add "GRAP revised 28 Sept 2026: pre-emptive Stage I" to your Delhi-NCR air-quality case study, with a cross-link to today's firecracker case (item 5).

articles.title: Supreme Court: no total firecracker ban, no 24-hour bursting — time-limited use is the middle path — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A clean case of the Court balancing fundamental rights against each other: religious and cultural practice (Art. 25) on one side, and health and a clean environment (Art. 21) on the other. It is a strong Mains example of judicial balancing and of the Court as environmental regulator.
**Memorise:** ***Arjun Gopal v. Union of India*** (W.P.(C) 728/2015), bench of **Justices M.M. Sundresh and Augustine George Masih**. The Court said it would not agree to a **total ban** and would not allow **unrestricted use**, and signalled **specified bursting hours** and limits on cracker types during festivals. It approved manufacture of **new-generation joint (series) crackers** subject to conditions (shell size and quantity limits, intervals between bursts) based on **CSIR-NEERI** specifications. **Barium** content in **Generation-2 green crackers** is being tested in **Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai**; the decision is **deferred to 15 Oct 2026**. Delhi-NCR restrictions run in the separate **M.C. Mehta** proceedings. Constitutional hooks: **Art. 21** (health, clean environment), **Art. 25(1)** (subject to public order, morality, health).
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary; Fundamental Rights); GS3 – Environment.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Fundamental Rights → Art. 21 and Art. 25*. *Nudge:* add "No total ban; time-bound use; barium test decision 15 Oct 2026" under your Art. 21 environmental-rights case list, and cross-link to the GRAP item above.

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare (CCEA): MSP for Rabi crops, Marketing Season 2027-28 approved — wheat only +₹25, oilseeds and pulses get bigger hikes (30 Sep)
articles.text:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs raised MSP for all six mandated rabi crops, keeping MSP at a minimum of 1.5 times the all-India weighted average cost of production. The tiny wheat hike and big oilseed/pulse hikes signal a push for crop diversification and import substitution (edible oils, pulses).

| Crop | MSP 2026-27 (₹/qtl) | MSP 2027-28 (₹/qtl) | Rise | Margin over cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheat | 2,585 | **2,610** | +25 | 106% |
| Barley | 2,150 | 2,286 | +136 | 58% |
| Gram | 5,875 | 5,958 | +83 | 59% |
| Lentil (Masur) | 7,000 | 7,390 | +390 | 92% |
| Rapeseed & Mustard | 6,200 | 6,613 | +413 | 96% |
| Safflower | 6,540 | **7,215** | **+675 (highest)** | 50% |

*Note:* The margin over cost is calculated on A2+FL cost; MSP is recommended by CACP. **Notebook: GS3 Agriculture / Economy.**

articles.title: Ministry of Power (Bureau of Energy Efficiency): CAFE-III — new Corporate Average Fuel Consumption norms for passenger cars for 2027-32 notified (30 Sep)
articles.text:
Fleet-average fuel-consumption standards for car makers for 1 Apr 2027 – 31 Mar 2032 (CAFE-III), under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, administered by BEE. Why it matters: cuts oil imports and CO₂, and nudges manufacturers towards EVs, hybrids and ethanol/CBG-compatible vehicles.

- Target: ~16.7% improvement in fleet fuel efficiency; benchmark tightens from **3.996 to 3.3273 litres/100 km** (2027-28 → 2031-32).
- Reference curb weight raised from 1,082 kg to 1,229 kg (eases burden on lighter cars).
- Super-credits for BEVs, plug-in hybrids, strong hybrids, flex-fuel; **Carbon Neutrality Factor** rewards ethanol blends and compressed biogas (CBG).
- Eligible fuel-saving technologies expanded from 4 to 12 (credit capped at 9.0 g CO₂/km); credit pooling/trading among manufacturers; buy-out mechanism; exemption for makers producing under 1,000 units/yr; dual reporting under MIDC and WLTP.

**Notebook: GS3 Environment / Energy / Economy.**

articles.title: Ministry of Mines: Auction of two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea launched (1 Oct)
articles.text:
India's first offshore-mineral auction attempt in 2024 (13 blocks) was cancelled; this is a fresh round of two blocks under composite licences (exploration + mining), under the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development & Regulation) Act, 2002 and Offshore Areas Mineral Auction Rules, 2024 (amended 2026).

- Blocks (per reports): **West Sewell Ridge-01** (~1,000 sq km, off Great Nicobar) and **Sewell Rise-01** (~632 sq km); polymetallic nodules/crusts — cobalt, copper, manganese, nickel.
- Rule change (24 Sep 2026): minimum technically-qualified bidders for a first-attempt auction cut from **three to two**, to reduce cancellation risk.
- Significance: critical-mineral security (EV batteries, renewables), Blue Economy, EEZ resource use alongside ISA/UNCLOS frameworks.

**Notebook: GS3 Economy (Mining, Critical Minerals) / GS1 Geography (Oceanic resources).**

articles.title: UIDAI (MeitY): Five new initiatives unveiled at 'Aadhaar Samvaad', Kolkata (30 Sep)
articles.text:
1. **Face authentication for ePDS** — with Dept. of Food & Public Distribution and NIC; alternative where fingerprints fail (worn prints, etc.).
2. **SWIK Portal 2.0** — single window for NGOs/entities to seek Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance approvals from ministries.
3. **Sub-AUA / Sub-KUA LITE framework** — cheaper, faster onboarding for low-volume entities using already-certified infrastructure.
4. **Token Management System** at UIDAI offices — queue/appointment management.
5. **Revamped website and careers portal** — BHASHINI-based multilingual support expanded from 13 to 23 languages.

**Notebook: GS2 Governance / e-Governance.**

### Scheme-in-focus: Rabi MSP / Price Support (Agriculture)
- **Ministry:** Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare; MSP recommended by CACP, approved by CCEA.
- **Objective:** assured remunerative prices; cropping-pattern correction.
- **Features:** 1.5× cost-of-production formula; covers 22 mandated crops (+FRP for sugarcane); procurement under PSS/PM-AASHA, with state agencies/FCI/NAFED.
- **Beneficiaries:** farmers across India; effective mostly for wheat/paddy in practice.
- **Significance:** low wheat hike reflects ample buffer stocks; oilseed/pulse tilt supports National Mission on Edible Oils and pulses self-reliance.

### Also worth a line (29 Sep – 1 Oct)
- Cabinet also approved a ₹1,789.52 crore Traffic Management System for Delhi (42 corridors, 1,092 adaptive signals, AI-based enforcement; 24-month build + 5-year O&M).
- Ministry of Agriculture: Viksit Krishi/Rabi Abhiyan 2026 — ₹1,200+ crore sanctioned to 10 States under PM-RKVY (per snippet reports; verify on PIB before citing).

articles.title: India sits at Pakistan's first SCO table: the Council of National Coordinators meets in Islamabad — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Relations with Pakistan are frozen, but India still goes to Pakistan-chaired SCO meetings. That split between multilateral and bilateral engagement is a strong Mains line. For Prelims, the testable facts are the structure of SCO bodies (which council meets when) and how the chairmanship rotates.
**Memorise:** The meeting ran from **28 to 30 Sept 2026** in Islamabad. It was the **Council of National Coordinators**, not a ministerial meeting. India's delegation was led by **MEA Additional Secretary Alok Dimri**. It is Pakistan's first major SCO event since it took the **2026–27 chairmanship from Kyrgyzstan on 1 Sept 2026**, after the Bishkek summit. The theme is ***"Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity."*** The **Heads of State summit is due in Islamabad in August 2027**. MEA says it will decide on PM Modi's attendance "at the appropriate time". India will host the **India–Central Asia Summit in 2027**. The last Indian ministerial visit was **EAM Jaishankar in October 2024** (SCO Council of Heads of Government), the first by an Indian foreign minister since 2015. The SCO now has **10 members**, the latest being Belarus. *Mains line:* "India uses the SCO to stay in the room without taking part in the bilateral."
**Notebook:** GS2 – IR (Regional groupings; India–Pakistan).
**Static anchor:** IR notes → *Regional & global groupings: SCO* (structure: Heads of State Council, Heads of Government Council, CFM, Council of National Coordinators; Secretariat in Beijing, RATS in Tashkent). *Nudge:* add a "Chair 2026–27: Pakistan (from Kyrgyzstan) → summit Islamabad, Aug 2027" row to your SCO chair timeline, and cross-link to your India–Central Asia note.

articles.title: Green Energy Corridor-III: ₹1.86 lakh crore for intra-state lines plus 50 GWh of batteries — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The constraint on renewable energy is shifting from building generation to evacuating and storing the power. This is the first GEC phase to put **battery storage inside the scheme**. It fits GS3 infrastructure and energy-transition questions and pairs well with the "curtailment" problem.
**Memorise:** Approved by the Union Cabinet on **30 Sept 2026**. Total outlay is **₹1,86,405 crore**:
- **₹1,36,378 crore** for **intra-state transmission (InSTS)**
- **₹50,000 crore** for **50 GWh of BESS**

Central Financial Assistance is **₹54,082 crore** (about 29% of the outlay). It will evacuate **135 GW** of RE, with completion by **FY 2032-33**. **Greenfield** InSTS goes through **Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB)**, with private providers building on a build-own-operate-maintain basis. **Brownfield** upgrades are on a **cost-plus** basis through the **State Transmission Utilities**. Targets it serves: **500 GW** non-fossil capacity by 2030 and **900 GW** by 2035. India's solar capacity was **162.15 GW** in June 2026. Background: **GEC-I** (2015, KfW-supported) and **GEC-II** (Jan 2022: about ₹12,031 crore, 33% CFA, 7 states, about 20 GW).
**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (Infrastructure: Energy) and Environment (Climate mitigation).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Economy, *Infrastructure → Power sector (Electricity Act 2003, CERC/SERC, transmission)*; Shankar IAS, *Renewable Energy*. *Nudge:* add a GEC-I → II → III comparison table (year, outlay, CFA, GW, storage) and cross-link to your "RE curtailment / grid-scale storage (BESS VGF, pumped storage)" note.

articles.title: India's first PRAMAAN certificates: a home-grown forest and wood certification label — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India now has its own certification route for sustainably managed plantations, agroforestry and bamboo. This matters for exporters facing due-diligence rules such as the **EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)**. It is a new Prelims term and a Mains example of "trees outside forests" and farmer livelihoods.
**Memorise:** On **30 Sept 2026**, Environment Minister **Bhupender Yadav** handed over the first certificates. **PRAMAAN** stands for *Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of sustainable Management practices for Agroforestry And Natural forestry resources*. It runs under the **Indian Forest & Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS)**, which MoEFCC launched in **Dec 2023**.
- **Operating agency:** **IIFM, Bhopal**
- **Audits:** third-party audits by **NABCB-accredited** certification bodies
- **Standard:** Indian Forest Management Standard under the **National Working Plan Code 2023**
- **First recipients:** **Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation** (about **33,000 ha** of plantations) and **Govind Mohapatra**, a farmer with the **Odisha Bamboo Development Agency**
- **International fit:** benchmarked against the major international certification frameworks to help exporters meet due-diligence rules such as the EUDR. Certification is **voluntary** (IFWCS was launched as a voluntary, market-based scheme).

**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (Forests; sustainable trade).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, *Forest / Agroforestry* chapter (India State of Forest Report, trees outside forests, Green India Mission). *Nudge:* add "IFWCS/PRAMAAN (IIFM, voluntary, EUDR link)" to your *environment certifications and labels* list, beside eco-mark, BEE star labels and GreenCo.

articles.title: Places in News: Vasundhara Tal (Chamoli) gets Uttarakhand's first glacial-lake early-warning system — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** GLOF risk in the Himalaya is a recurring Geography and Disaster Management theme. This item moves it from mapping lakes to instrumenting them. Pair it with the Chamoli disaster of Feb 2021 and the Sikkim South Lhonak GLOF of Oct 2023.
**Memorise:** Installation runs from **29 Sept to 15 Oct 2026**. It was flagged off by Chief Secretary **Anand Bardhan** and is coordinated by the **USDMA**. Other agencies: **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (Dehradun)**, **CBRI (Roorkee)**, **SDRF, NDRF and ITBP**. Equipment:
- water-level sensors
- automatic weather stations (temperature, pressure)
- snow-depth sensors
- **eight sub-surface temperature probes**
- satellite links for real-time alerts

Uttarakhand has **344 glacial lakes**, of which **13 are high-risk** (2023 data): **Pithoragarh 6, Chamoli 4, and one each in Bageshwar, Tehri Garhwal and Uttarkashi**. Vasundhara Tal is a **pilot**, and similar systems are planned for other lakes.
**Notebook:** GS1 – Geography (Glacial landforms; Places in News); GS3 – Disaster Management.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class 11 *India: Physical Environment*, ch. *Natural Hazards and Disasters*; NCERT Class 11 *Fundamentals of Physical Geography*, ch. *Landforms and their Evolution* (glaciers, moraines). *Nudge:* mark Vasundhara Tal (Chamoli) and the Pithoragarh cluster on your Uttarakhand map, and add "instrumented EWS (2026)" to your NDMA GLOF-mitigation note.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: First PRAMAAN certificates issued under India's own forest and wood certification scheme (29 Sep)
articles.text:
**What it is:** Union Environment Minister **Bhupender Yadav** presented the first certificates under **PRAMAAN**, the label of the **Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS)**. The Ministry launched the scheme in **December 2023**. The first two certificates went to:
- the **Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC)**, for about **33,000 ha** of plantations;
- **Govind Mohapatra**, an individual bamboo farmer linked to the **Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA)**.

**Why it matters:** Buyers such as the EU now require proof that timber and wood products are **deforestation-free** (see the **EU Deforestation Regulation, EUDR**). Until now, Indian producers depended on foreign private labels such as FSC and PEFC for this proof. PRAMAAN is a government-backed domestic alternative with third-party audits. It covers **trees outside forests (agroforestry)**, which is where much of India's wood supply comes from, and it aims to include smallholders, bamboo growers and women's SHGs.

**Key facts:**
- **Full form:** Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of sustainable Management practices for Agroforestry And Natural forestry resources.
- **Scheme operator:** **Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal**, under MoEFCC.
- **Three certification streams:** (i) **Forest Management (FM)**, (ii) **Trees Outside Forests (TOF) Management**, (iii) **Chain of Custody (CoC)**, which gives traceability through the supply chain.
- **Standard:** the Indian Forest Management Standard, part of the **National Working Plan Code (NWPC) 2023**. Audits are done by independent certification bodies accredited by the **National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB)**, not by self-declaration.
- The scheme is benchmarked against international certification frameworks so that certified products can meet export due-diligence rules.

**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (forest conservation, agroforestry, trade–environment linkages). GS2 – IR (EUDR as a non-tariff measure).

articles.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment: "Shram Samvad" — 90-day awareness campaign on the four Labour Codes across 316 districts (28 Sep)
articles.text:
**What it is:** Labour Minister **Mansukh Mandaviya** announced **Shram Samvad** at the CII–EFI National Conference on Industrial Relations in New Delhi. Ministry teams will visit **industrial clusters in 316 districts across all 36 States/UTs over 90 days**. They will meet industry, lawyers, chartered accountants and other intermediaries to clear up confusion about the new labour-law framework. The Minister said stakeholders are still confused about the Codes.

**Why it matters:** The Codes are law, but implementing them depends on States framing their own rules and on employers actually complying. Shram Samvad shows the Ministry moving to outreach and consultation to close that implementation gap. This is useful GS2 material on how a law's design differs from its implementation, and on labour as a Concurrent List subject.

**Key facts:**
- **The four Codes:** Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Code on Social Security, 2020; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Together they consolidated **29 central labour laws**.
- **Figures cited by the Ministry:** social-security coverage rose from **19% (2015) to 68%** of the population (about **101 crore** people). Employment elasticity was about **1.11** for 2017–23.
- Released at the event: an **"Employer's Guide under the New Labour Codes Framework: Fixed-Term Employment in India"**.
- Labour Secretary **Chandra Bhushan Kumar** said the **National Classification of Occupations** is being updated to add emerging roles, including AI-related jobs.

**Notebook:** GS2 – Governance (implementation of legislation, Centre–State roles). GS3 – Economy (employment, labour reforms, informal sector).

articles.title: Ministry of Steel: Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) set up as an apex safety body, backed by a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (28–30 Sep)
The Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for the Supreme Court — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** This is the first batch of elevations since Parliament raised the Court's strength to 38. It also brings the appointment machinery back into focus: the Judges Cases, the Memorandum of Procedure, seniority and diversity.
**Memorise:** On **28 Sept 2026** the Collegium (**CJI Surya Kant** with Justices Vikram Nath, B.V. Nagarathna, M.M. Sundresh and P.S. Narasimha) recommended **Justice Sunita Agarwal** (CJ, Gujarat HC; parent HC Allahabad), **Justice D.K. Upadhyaya** (CJ, Delhi HC; from Allahabad) and **Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh** (CJ, Telangana HC; parent HC Jharkhand). The SC's working strength is **34 against a sanctioned 38**. If these three are appointed, it becomes **37 with one vacancy**. The strength went from 34 to 38 (CJI + 37) through the **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026**, which got presidential assent on 12 Aug 2026 and replaced the May 2026 Ordinance. Justice Agarwal would make **three women judges** on the SC. None of the three is in line to become CJI. *Mains line:* "Adding benches only helps if appointments keep pace. Sanctioned strength means little without timely elevations."
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Supreme Court* chapter → Composition (Art. 124(1): Parliament fixes the number by law) and Appointment of Judges (the Judges Cases). *Nudge:* change "34" to "38 (2026 Amendment Act)" in your notes and add this batch as a live example beside the Second/Third/Fourth Judges Cases.

articles.title: A single digital portal for livestock insurance under the National Livestock Mission — Agriculture
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Risk management for livestock-dependent households is weaker than for crops. PMFBY has a mature digital system, but livestock cover was paper-heavy and prone to fraud. It fits GS3 questions on animal husbandry, rural income diversification and "digital public infrastructure in agriculture".
**Memorise:** Union Minister **Rajiv Ranjan (Lalan) Singh** launched it in New Delhi on **28 Sept 2026**. It is run by the **Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying** as a web workflow under **NLM (Risk Management & Insurance)** and covers everything from policy issue to claim settlement. The farmer pays **15%** of the premium. The other **85%** is shared by the Centre and the States in a **60:40** ratio, or **90:10** in the Himalayan and North-Eastern States. The subsidised cap is **10 cattle units per household**, with a separate **5-unit** cap for pigs and rabbits. Covered animals: indigenous and crossbred cattle, **buffalo, horse, donkey, camel, sheep, goat, pig, rabbit, yak, mithun**. It works in **13 languages** (11 regional plus Hindi and English) and links to the **Bharat Pashudhan** database and the **12-digit ear-tag ID** to stop duplicate policies. RFID tagging is under consideration. In the last five years, **60.8 lakh animals were insured** and **₹161.07 crore** was paid in claims.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Agriculture (Animal husbandry; agri-insurance).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Agriculture pillar, *Animal husbandry schemes (NLM, Rashtriya Gokul Mission, NADCP)*. *Nudge:* add a "Crop vs livestock insurance" comparison row (PMFBY 2%/1.5%/5% farmer share vs 15% under NLM).

articles.title: Foundation stone for India's first port-based e-methanol plant at Kandla — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** This is how India's green-hydrogen push is supposed to become an export product: a green marine fuel sold as bunkers on the Asia–Europe route. It is useful for questions on e-fuels, shipping decarbonisation and the National Green Hydrogen Mission. For a Physics-optional student it is also a clean electrolysis → CO₂-hydrogenation chain. *(This is a different story from the 28 Sept mega-port notification, even though Deendayal features in both.)*
**Memorise:** The foundation stone was laid on **28 Sept 2026** by Union Minister **Sarbananda Sonowal** with the CMs of **Gujarat** and **Assam**. The plant is at **Deendayal Port Authority (DPA), Kandla**, with capacity of **150 TPD** at a cost of **₹2,300 crore**. It is a JV of **DPA (76%)** and **Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (24%)**. **Phase I** is 50 TPD for ₹1,200 crore (target Jan 2027) and **Phase II** is 100 TPD for ₹1,100 crore (target Mar 2027). Feedstock: **renewable power + water (→ green H₂) + biogenic CO₂**. The target production cost is about **US$750/t**, against a global price of about **US$1,300/t**, and the plant is expected to create **3,500+ jobs**. Chemistry: CO₂ + 3H₂ → CH₃OH + H₂O. The fuel is "carbon-neutral" only because the CO₂ is biogenic. It still emits CO₂ when burnt.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Sci-Tech (Energy) and Environment (Climate mitigation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, *Renewable Energy / Climate change mitigation*; NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, *Hydrogen* (production by electrolysis). *Nudge:* add "e-methanol / e-fuels" under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (Jan 2023, ₹19,744 crore, 5 MMT by 2030) and cross-link to the Deendayal green-hydrogen-hub note.

articles.title: Japan asks the UN to delete "enemy state" clauses from the Charter — and China and Russia say no — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** In her UNGA-81 address, Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi called the Charter's wartime "enemy state" language obsolete. It links three UPSC staples: UN Charter architecture, P5 veto over amendments, and UNSC reform (India and Japan are G4 partners). Fresh hook: Japan–China friction over Taiwan; both Beijing and Moscow object.
**Memorise:** Articles **53, 77, 107** = "enemy state" clauses (Axis states of WWII; allowed action against them without Security Council authorisation). UNGA declared them obsolete in **1995 (Res 50/52)**; the **2005 World Summit Outcome** recorded the intent to delete them, but no formal amendment has happened. Amendment route = **Art. 108** (two-thirds of GA + ratification by two-thirds of members including **all five P5**). *Mains line:* "A Charter frozen in 1945 cannot serve a 2026 order — yet only the P5 can unfreeze it."
**Notebook:** GS2 – IR (UN & reforms).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth-style IR shelf → *UN system / Charter (Chs. VII, XVIII)*; Shankar/Mrunal IR pillar "UNSC reform". *Nudge:* add a cross-link from "UNSC reform / G4" to Art. 108 and to this enemy-state clause note.

articles.title: TDB puts ₹200 crore behind Agnikul's fully reusable Agnibaan — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Reusability is the next space-economy frontier (post-IN-SPACe, private launchers). Note the *instrument*: funding via the **Optionally Convertible Debentures**, drawn from the **RDI (Research Development & Innovation) fund**, to lift the technology from **TRL-4 to TRL-8**. A clean way to remember what TRL means.
**Memorise:** Signed by Technology Development Board (statutory body under DST) with Agnikul Cosmos (Chennai). Targets: full-system reuse (not just first stage), lightweight upper stage, **semi-cryogenic** liquid propulsion with deep throttling and restart, controlled descent and recovery. Agnikul earlier built the single-piece 3D-printed engine ("Agnilet"). Benefits stressed: lower cost per launch, high cadence, less space debris. Reported alongside: GalaxEye ≈ ₹63.84 crore.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Sci-Tech (Space).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum/Mrunal *Space technology* → launch vehicles (expendable vs reusable), cryogenic vs semi-cryogenic; IN-SPACe/NSIL cross-link. *Nudge:* add a "TRL 1–9" mini-table and the RDI scheme to your S&T innovation-financing page.

articles.title: Four "mega ports" notified for the first time — Economy (Infrastructure/Logistics)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A new tier in India's port hierarchy created under the **Indian Ports Act, 2025**. Expect questions on Sagarmala/maritime vision, competitive private ports, and Union vs State ports (Entry 27, Union List).
**Memorise:** Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways notified **Deendayal (Kandla), JNPA (Nhava Sheva), Paradip and Mundra** under **Section 73**. Reported criteria: about **150 million tonnes/yr** of cargo (bulk) or **7.5 million TEU** (container); status reviewed periodically (reported: 5 years). **Mundra is the only privately operated** one of the four; India has **12 major ports** and 200+ non-major ports. *Flag: criteria and 5-year validity are from secondary reports; the Gazette text was not accessible in this run.*
**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (Infrastructure: ports).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh *Infrastructure → Ports*; Mrunal "Sagarmala". *Nudge:* update your "Major Port Authorities Act 2021 → Indian Ports Act 2025" line and add a 4-port mega-port list.

articles.title: Karnataka rejects the Western Ghats ESA draft again — and asks for a year to do ground surveys — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** *Not a repeat of the 20 Sept ESZ story — that was about Eco-Sensitive Zones around protected areas; this is the Western Ghats ESA under the Gadgil–Kasturirangan track.* New sub-development: Karnataka's Assembly unanimously rejected the latest draft (**seventh draft ESA notification, 27 July 2026**, as reported) and wants a plot-level physical survey. Classic conservation-vs-livelihood, federalism (land is a State subject) and remote-sensing-vs-ground-truth case.
**Memorise:** Reported Karnataka portion: **~20,668 sq km, 1,449 villages, 10 districts**; the overall draft is reported as **~56,825 sq km across six states** (figures vary slightly across sources — verify before quoting). Karnataka's objections: satellite-based boundaries, whole villages included for ~one-fifth forest cover, unresolved forest-rights/land issues. Background: **Gadgil (WGEEP, 2011)** = whole Ghats ESA in three zones; **Kasturirangan HLWG (2013)** = ~**37%** of the Ghats as ESA. ESA drafts are issued under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (Conservation, Western Ghats); GS1 – Geography.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS *Environment → Conservation efforts in India*; NCERT/Spectrum *Western Ghats*. *Nudge:* add a Gadgil vs Kasturirangan comparison row and cross-link to "UNESCO WHS: Western Ghats (2012)".

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: National Agriculture Conference — Rabi Abhiyan 2026 begins at Pusa, New Delhi (28–29 Sep)
articles.text:
**What it is:** The annual pre-season Centre–State conference to finalise the Rabi crop plan. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan stressed **data-based planning and Centre–State partnership**, and named the **"water budget"** as the most critical parameter — states should assess irrigation availability and prefer **pulses and oilseeds** where water is limited. He flagged drought stress across roughly two-thirds of Maharashtra and parts of Karnataka; central assessment teams are to visit by **3 October**.

**Why it matters:** Sets input planning (seed, fertiliser, credit) for the Rabi season and pushes crop diversification away from water-guzzling cereals; also shows the drought-assessment machinery in action.

**Key facts:**
- Themes: self-reliance and diversification; sustainability and climate-friendly farming; digital agriculture, infrastructure, finance and risk management.
- Day 2 agenda: rainfall forecast, fertiliser availability, digital farming and **farmer registries**, pulses and oilseeds missions, institutional marketing.

**Notebook:** GS3 – Agriculture (cropping patterns, water use, food security, drought).

articles.title: Jaishankar's UNGA-81 statement: the Indus Waters Treaty goes on the UN record, and India co-founds a shipping-safety group — International Relations
articles.text:
**What's new since the 21 Sept preview:** India delivered its national statement on **26 September 2026**. Two things in it are new for your notes. India defended keeping the **Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance** from the UNGA podium. India also joined **Liberia** and about two dozen partners to launch a **Group of Friends on the Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers**.

**Exam angle:** This is India's first statement at the General Assembly that ties a water treaty directly to cross-border terrorism. The line was that "friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism", and that understandings premised on good faith "will naturally be called into question". For Mains, use it on how far treaty obligations stand when there is a security threat (IR / GS2). The shipping group adds to India's maritime-security material alongside the Red Sea attacks, SAGAR/MAHASAGAR and the IMO.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Speech: 26 Sept 2026, 81st UNGA General Debate. Lines to quote: "Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised". He called Pakistan a "serial practitioner of terrorism".
- IWT stays **in abeyance** (in place since April 2025, after Pahalgam) "until Pakistan … credibly and irrevocably ends its support for cross-border … terrorism".
- **IWT basics:** signed **1960, Karachi**, by **Nehru and Ayub Khan**, with the **World Bank** as a signatory. **Eastern rivers** (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) go to India. **Western rivers** (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) go to Pakistan, and India has limited non-consumptive uses such as run-of-river hydro. Disputes pass through the **Permanent Indus Commission**, then a Neutral Expert, then a Court of Arbitration.
- Shipping: "the targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers … is simply unacceptable". **Liberia** is one of the world's largest flag-registries, so a flag state is co-leading the group.
- Other lines from the speech: the "**4F crisis**" in the Global South (food, fuel, fertiliser, finance); "endless war must give way to an end to war" (on Ukraine).

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — IR (India–Pakistan; Important international groupings). GS3 link: water security.

**Static anchor:** Your GS2 India–Neighbourhood file (India–Pakistan → IWT). Cross-link to *Spectrum / NCERT Geography — Indus river system*. **Nudge:** add a box showing "IWT: Eastern vs Western rivers + three-tier dispute ladder", and link it to the 21 Sept UNGA card.

articles.title: Centre cuts FY27 gross borrowing by ₹1.2 lakh crore — H2 calendar set at ₹7.86 lakh crore — Economy
articles.text:
**Headline:** On 25 September 2026 the Finance Ministry, after consulting the RBI, announced that it will raise **₹7.86 lakh crore through dated securities in October–March (H2 FY27)**. FY27 gross market borrowing falls to about **₹15.99 lakh crore**, down from the Budget estimate of **₹17.2 lakh crore**.

**Exam angle:** The cut is mostly a **debt-management move, not a fiscal saving**. The government **switched ₹1,14,286 crore of G-secs maturing in FY27** into longer-dated papers, which lowers this year's redemption bill. The item tests G-sec vocabulary that Prelims likes: **dated securities vs T-bills, switch operations, Ways and Means Advances (WMA), Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs)**. In Mains, use it for fiscal consolidation and for how public debt management affects bond yields and crowding-out.

**Facts to memorise:**
- H2 borrowing is **₹7.86 lakh crore** over **23 weekly auctions**, with tenors of **3 to 50 years**. The 10-year tenor has the largest share (**26.3%**), then 15-year (**17.6%**) and 5-year (**12.1%**).
- Total reduction is **₹1,20,494 crore** against the BE, driven mainly by the **₹1,14,286 crore switch**. H1 borrowing works out to roughly ₹8.1 lakh crore (derived figure).
- **SGrBs: ₹15,000 crore** in H2. They are *part of* gross market borrowing, and the proceeds are earmarked for green projects.
- **T-bills (Q3):** about **₹23,000 crore a week** across 91-, 182- and 364-day bills.
- **WMA limit for H2: ₹50,000 crore.** WMA are temporary RBI advances to cover mismatches between receipts and payments. Using them beyond the limit counts as an overdraft.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (Government Budgeting / Public Debt / Money Market).

**Static anchor:** *Mrunal — Pillar #1B (Banking) and #2 (Budget, Fiscal Policy — public debt)*; *Spectrum/Ramesh Singh — "Money market & capital market" (G-secs, T-bills)*. **Nudge:** update your "G-sec toolkit" table with a row for **Switch = swap short-maturity paper for long; lowers current-year redemptions; gross borrowing falls, debt stock does not**.

articles.title: TRAI launches the Digital Connectivity Rating (DCR) Platform — indoor signal quality becomes a certified property attribute — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Headline:** On **25 September 2026** TRAI Chairman **Anil Kumar Lahoti** launched the **DCR Platform** (portal plus mobile app, at dcrp.trai.gov.in). It digitises the rating of buildings for indoor digital connectivity.

**Exam angle:** Around **70–80% of mobile data is used indoors**, and 5G's higher frequencies pass through walls poorly. Connectivity is now being treated like an **energy-efficiency label**. The idea is that market pressure will make builders plan **Digital Connectivity Infrastructure (DCI)** at the design stage, including fibre ducts and in-building solutions (IBS). Use it for GS3 infrastructure and digital-divide answers, and in Prelims to identify the regulator.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Legal basis: **TRAI (Rating of Properties for Digital Connectivity) Regulations, 2024** (Oct 2024), amended **13 May 2026**. **Rating Manual 2026** was issued on **9 June 2026**.
- Ratings are given by accredited **Digital Connectivity Rating Agencies (DCRAs)**. TRAI approved the first **eight** in Aug 2025.
- Parameters: **fibre readiness, 4G/5G mobile coverage, in-building solutions and Wi-Fi**, measured in common areas, lifts and basements.
- Features: ratings for **under-construction and completed** properties, **Aadhaar eSign** certificates with **QR verification**, and public search by property, certificate ID or location. **Participation is opt-in**, which critics call its main weakness.
- TRAI: statutory body under the **TRAI Act, 1997**, set up **20 Feb 1997**. Disputes go to **TDSAT**.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Sci-Tech / Infrastructure (Telecom). GS2 link: regulatory bodies.

**Static anchor:** *Mrunal — Pillar #5 (Infrastructure: telecom)*; your GS2 "Statutory/Regulatory bodies" sheet (TRAI vs TDSAT). **Nudge:** add DCR next to BEE star labelling under "information-disclosure regulation", which works by shaping behaviour through labels.

articles.title: Places in News: Tigray — TPLF seizes Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports, and the Pretoria peace deal is fraying — Geography
articles.text:
**Headline:** From **23 September 2026** forces of the **Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)** seized the **Mekelle, Axum and Shire** airports and announced a "defensive war". **Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights** to all three. Fighting has spread into **Amhara and Afar**. A seven-group anti-government alliance announced on 21 September includes **Fano** militias and the **Oromo Liberation Army**, and there are reports of Eritrean support.

**Exam angle:** This is a Places-in-News map drill for the **Horn of Africa**, which sits next to the **Bab el-Mandeb** and the Red Sea shipping route. India has a direct stake: Ethiopia is a **BRICS member (since 1 Jan 2024)**, it hosts the **African Union HQ (Addis Ababa)**, and it is a major destination for Indian investment and lines of credit. The **Pretoria Agreement (Nov 2022)**, brokered by the AU, ended a war that the AU estimates killed about **6 lakh** people.

**Facts to memorise:**
- **Landlocked** since **Eritrea's independence (1993)**. Six neighbours: **Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan, Sudan**. Most trade goes through **Djibouti**.
- **Lake Tana** is the source of the **Blue Nile (Abay)**. **GERD** is on the Blue Nile. Ethiopia is called the "water tower of East Africa".
- **Danakil Depression (Afar)**, part of the **Great Rift Valley**, is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth. The **Tekeze** river forms part of the Tigray–Amhara boundary zone.
- **Axum** (Aksum) was the seat of the ancient Aksumite kingdom and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. **Mekelle** is Tigray's capital.

**Destination notebook:** GS1 — Geography (Places in News: Africa). GS2 link: India–Africa.

**Static anchor:** *NCERT Class XI "Fundamentals of Physical Geography" — plate tectonics / rift valleys*; atlas work on the Horn of Africa. **Nudge:** mark Mekelle, Axum, Shire, Lake Tana, the Danakil Depression and Djibouti port on your Africa blank map, and cross-link to the 13 Sept Perim Island / Bab el-Mandeb card.

articles.title: Election Commission of India: Full Commission decides on SIR document collection, ECINet audit and new transparency rules; claims deadlines extended for Delhi and Maharashtra
articles.text:
On **26 September 2026**, the full Commission met: CEC **Gyanesh Kumar** and Election Commissioners **S.S. Sandhu** and **Vivek Joshi**. It issued a set of decisions on the ongoing **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of electoral rolls. The meeting followed press reports of dissent inside the Commission. The ECI says every SIR decision, starting with the **24 June 2025** order that began the exercise, was **unanimous**.

**Why it matters:** This is a live case study in how a multi-member constitutional body governs itself under **Article 324**. It connects to voter-roll integrity, the risk of exclusion, and the ECI's own internal procedures. All three are standard GS2 Mains themes.

**Key decisions**
- **Doorstep collection:** For "unmapped" electors, **BLOs will collect documents at home** and upload them to **ECINet** for the ERO to decide. A hearing will be held only in exceptional cases, **preferably online**, and a family member can represent the elector.
- **Inclusion:** DEOs must set up **help desks and special camps** for the homeless, labourers and economically weaker voters.
- **Form 6:** The Commission noted that the Supreme Court has upheld the Form 6 declaration used during SIR. Outside SIR periods, the regular forms under the **Registration of Electors Rules, 1960** apply.
- **ECINet audit:** A committee headed by the **Senior Deputy Election Commissioner**, with an **independent IIT/IIIT expert**, will check whether ECINet complies with electoral law and rules.
- **Deadlines extended:** **Delhi**: claims and objections until **30 October 2026**, disposal until **30 November**. **Maharashtra**: claims and objections until **12 October**, disposal until **10 November**.
- **Internal governance:** Agendas will be circulated before Commission meetings and minutes issued afterwards. APARs must be completed by **31 December** each year, and officers need prior approval for foreign trips.
- According to the release, **SIR has been completed in 20 States/UTs**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — Polity (ECI, Article 324, electoral rolls, RP Act 1950).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: Interest-free working capital of ₹50,000 per barn for FCV tobacco farmers in Andhra Pradesh
articles.text:
On **25 September 2026**, the Centre approved an **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme** for **Flue-Cured Virginia (FCV) tobacco** growers in **Andhra Pradesh**. The government linked the move to weaker global demand, geopolitical developments and shifts in international trade. About **100 million kg** of FCV tobacco had been auctioned in the **2025-26 season**, which opened on **25 March 2026**.

**Why it matters:** This is a textbook conflict for Mains. Farm-income distress in a crop whose exports earn foreign exchange sits against India's public-health commitments under the **WHO FCTC**. Article 17 of the FCTC asks parties to promote economically viable alternatives to tobacco growing.

### Scheme-in-focus: **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme (FCV tobacco, Andhra Pradesh)**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce). Tobacco is a commercial crop regulated by the **Tobacco Board** (a statutory body under the Tobacco Board Act, 1975, headquartered in **Guntur**).
- **Objective:** Give immediate liquidity to growers hit by slow sales in a weak market.
- **Key features:** (i) **₹50,000 per curing barn**, **interest-free**; (ii) paid by **DBT** into farmers' accounts; (iii) meant for repaying institutional loans, household needs and next-season inputs; (iv) aims to cut dependence on private moneylenders.
- **Beneficiaries/coverage:** About **44,000 farmers**, with a total outlay of about **₹220 crore**.
- **Significance:** A targeted, time-bound liquidity measure rather than a price support. Useful as an example of how trade shocks pass through to farm incomes.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Agriculture (commercial crops, farm credit); cross-tag GS2 Health (FCTC).

articles.title: A *dua* is not a religious appeal: Supreme Court leaves the Malegaon Central election standing — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Headline:** On **25 September 2026** a Bench of **Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih** dismissed the appeal of SP candidate Shaan E Hind Nihal Ahmed and upheld the **Bombay High Court's 8 June 2026** rejection of his election petition against AIMIM's **Mufti Mohammad Ismail Abdul Khalique** (Malegaon Central, Maharashtra, Nov 2024 election).

**Exam angle:** The cleanest live case on **Section 123(3), Representation of the People Act, 1951** — appeal to vote on grounds of religion as a "corrupt practice". The courts separated a religious *ritual* at a campaign gathering (the audience saying "Ameen") from an actual *appeal to vote* on religious grounds, and found the petition lacked the "material facts" a corrupt-practice charge needs. Read it against *Abhiram Singh* (2017), which read the section very broadly.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Margin in the original result: **162 votes** (1,09,653 vs 1,09,491); the petitioner himself polled 9,624.
- HC held: performing *dua* ≠ soliciting votes on religion; surrogates' speeches, support from religious organisations and general religious references in pamphlets did not make out **s.123(3) or s.123(4)**; petition dismissed **without trial** for want of material facts.
- Procedure: election petitions are tried by the **High Court** (s.80A), filed within **45 days** of the result (s.81); appeal lies to the **Supreme Court** (s.116A). A proven corrupt practice voids the election (s.100(1)(b)) and can lead to disqualification (s.8A).
- *Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen* (2017), 7-judge Bench, **4:3** — "his religion" in s.123(3) covers the religion of the candidate, the agent **and the voter**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — Polity (Elections / Representation of the People Act).

**Static anchor:** *Laxmikanth*, "Elections" and "Electoral Reforms" chapters (RPA 1951 — corrupt practices and election disputes). **Nudge:** add a two-column box, "What *Abhiram Singh* bars / what *Malegaon* (2026) permits", and cross-link to Art. 329(b) (election disputes only by election petition).

articles.title: India–New Zealand FTA gets its start date: 20 October 2026 — International Relations
articles.text:
**Headline:** Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced (22 Sept) that the **India–New Zealand FTA** — concluded 22 Dec 2025, signed in New Delhi on **27 April 2026** — enters into force on **20 October 2026**.

**Exam angle:** A textbook of India's new-generation FTA design: **100% duty-free access** for Indian exports, a **carve-out for dairy** (the Fonterra question that sank RCEP for India), a **binding investment pledge**, and a mobility window. Good for GS2 (Indo-Pacific / Pacific partners) and GS3 (trade policy, protecting smallholders).

**Facts to memorise:**
- India's exports get **zero duty on 100% of tariff lines** in NZ; India liberalises about **70% of its tariff lines**, covering about **95% of bilateral trade value**.
- **Excluded by India:** dairy (milk, cream, whey, yoghurt, cheese, butterfat), plus onions, chickpeas, peas, maize, almonds, sugar. NZ gains on kiwifruit, apples, wool, sheep meat, forestry.
- **Investment:** NZ commits to facilitating **US$20 billion over 15 years** — India's **second** FTA with an FDI pledge after the **EFTA TEPA** (US$100 bn/15 yrs).
- **Mobility:** a quota of **5,000** temporary employment visas for skilled Indians (stays of up to 3 years), including yoga instructors, chefs and AYUSH practitioners; post-study work visas for Indian graduates. Also a bilateral **safeguard mechanism** and strict Rules of Origin.
- Merchandise trade is small (≈ US$1.15 bn in 2025-26); the target is to double goods-and-services trade in about five years.
- *Companion IR lines (defence diplomacy, same week):* **Ex VARUNA** (India–France navies; 24th edition) — **INS Trishul** reached **Toulon** on 22 Sept; **Ex NOMADIC ELEPHANT** (India–Mongolia army; **18th** edition) under way at **Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — International Relations (India & Oceania) + GS3 Economy (External sector / trade agreements).

**Static anchor:** *Mrunal* Economy — external sector pillar (FTAs, RoO, safeguards). **Nudge:** update your FTA table (Mauritius CECPA, UAE CEPA, Australia ECTA, EFTA TEPA, UK CETA, Oman, NZ) with a column for "dairy excluded?" and "investment pledge?".

articles.title: The sixth report card for India's tiger reserves — and waste is now graded — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline:** Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched the **6th cycle of the Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR 2026)** at an inception workshop in New Delhi on **25 September 2026**. It will cover **all 58 tiger reserves** and, for the first time, grade **solid waste management** as a separate criterion.

**Exam angle:** Tiger *numbers* are the headline Prelims fact, but MEE is UPSC's "governance of Protected Areas" hook. It shows how India audits conservation outcomes (IUCN-WCPA framework) rather than just counting animals. Previous cycles flagged climate action as the weakest area, which works well in a Mains answer.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Conducted by **NTCA with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** through independent multidisciplinary teams.
- Framework: **IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas (WCPA)** — six elements: **Context, Planning, Inputs, Process, Outputs, Outcomes**.
- Past cycles: **2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022**, rising from 28 to **51** reserves. In 2022, **Periyar (Kerala)** topped (~94%), followed by Satpura, Bandipur and Nagarhole; 12 reserves were rated "Excellent", none "Poor"; "carbon capture and climate change" scored lowest.
- New criterion covers waste from **forest chowkis, tourism and wildlife rescue centres**.
- Context: 3,682 tigers (AITE 2022), about 75% of the world's wild tigers; an estimated 35–40% live **outside** reserves (hence the "Tigers Outside Tiger Reserves" pilot in 40 forest divisions).

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Environment (Biodiversity conservation / Protected Areas).

**Static anchor:** *Shankar IAS*, "Protected Area Network" and "Project Tiger" chapters. **Nudge:** next to your tiger-reserve list, add a line on "how reserves are evaluated (MEE)" versus "how tigers are counted (AITE, every 4 years)". The two are often confused.

articles.title: ₹810.79 crore for 160 SAT-SAAW — DRDO's airfield-killer glide bomb goes into series order — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Headline:** On **23 September 2026** the Ministry of Defence signed a **₹810.79-crore** contract with **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)** for **160 Satellite-guided Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW)** for the IAF, under the **Buy (Indian-IDDM)** category.

**Exam angle:** A clean example of a DRDO design going into series production with a DPSU, meaning lab-to-line indigenisation under DAP-2020. It also shows the doctrinal shift to **stand-off precision strike**, where a pilot can hit runways, radars and bunkers without flying into the enemy's air defences.

**Facts to memorise:**
- **Developer:** DRDO — **Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad**. **Production:** BDL.
- **125-kg class** precision-guided **glide** weapon; stand-off range **up to ~100 km** (DRDO, 2021 test); targets runways, taxiways, radars, bunkers.
- Platforms: **Jaguar, Hawk and Su-30MKI**. It was flight-tested from HAL's **Hawk-i** in Jan 2021 off Odisha (9th successful trial).
- About **60% indigenous content**, with plans to indigenise the IMU, long-impact-delay fuse and twin store carrier. Deliveries **2027-28 and 2028-29**.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Science & Technology (Defence technology) / Internal Security (defence indigenisation).

**Static anchor:** Your defence-tech list of DRDO missiles and bombs (Astra, Rudram, SAAW, Pralay, Nirbhay). **Nudge:** add a "DAP-2020 procurement categories" line (Buy Indian-IDDM > Buy Indian > Buy & Make Indian > Buy & Make > Buy Global) and tag SAT-SAAW as IDDM.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (DPIIT): Make in India completes 12 years — PIB stocktake of manufacturing, FDI and PLI outcomes
articles.text:
Make in India was launched on **25 September 2014** to turn India into a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. On its 12th anniversary, the government put out a consolidated scorecard, and the Prime Minister summed it up as "more made in India, more investment, more exports".

**Why it matters:** This is the government's own balance sheet for its flagship industrial policy. Mains questions on deindustrialisation, PLI effectiveness and "Make in India vs. import dependence" need these baseline numbers. The release also shows the policy's new shape: sector-specific incentives such as PLI, semiconductors and rare-earth magnets now sit on top of the original ease-of-doing-business agenda.

**Key facts**
- Now called **Make in India 2.0**, it covers **27 sectors (15 manufacturing + 12 services)**.
- **Cumulative FDI of about US$ 843 billion** from 2014-15 to 2025-26.
- **Electronics production** rose from **₹1.9 lakh crore (2014-15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025-26)**. India is the **world's 2nd-largest mobile phone manufacturer**.
- **Defence production** rose from **₹46,429 crore (2014-15) to ₹1.78 lakh crore (2025-26)**. **Crude steel** rose from **81.7 MT to 170 MT**, and India has been the 2nd-largest producer since 2018.
- **PLI schemes** cover **14 sectors**. Reported production and sales exceed **₹22 lakh crore** and jobs exceed **14 lakh** (sources give slightly different cut-off figures).
- Enablers: the **National Single Window System** (327 Central + 3,452 State approvals), the **India Industrial Land Bank** (4,220 parks mapped), **PM GatiShakti** and **Startup India** (about 2.54 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups).

### Initiative-in-focus: **Make in India**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry, through **DPIIT**. **Launched:** 25 September 2014.
- **Objective:** Promote investment, foster innovation, build skills and create world-class manufacturing infrastructure.
- **Key features:** (i) four pillars: new processes, new infrastructure, new sectors and a new mindset; (ii) liberalised FDI, with the automatic route in most sectors; (iii) regulatory simplification through NSWS and ease-of-doing-business reforms; (iv) since 2020, sector-specific **PLI schemes** plus semiconductor and electronics-component missions.
- **Coverage:** 27 sectors under Make in India 2.0.
- **Significance:** Measures both the *scale* of output gains (electronics, defence, steel) and the *open questions* around domestic value addition and manufacturing's share of GDP. Use it to write a balanced Mains answer.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (industrial policy, manufacturing, FDI).

articles.title: Ministry of Tourism: World Tourism Day 2026 — theme "Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism"; PIB releases a sector backgrounder
articles.text:
The Ministry of Tourism issued a backgrounder on **26 September 2026** ahead of **World Tourism Day (27 September)**. The global host this year is **El Salvador**. India's national ceremony in New Delhi is slated to launch a **National Digital Tourism Stack** and **Dekho Apna Desh 2.0**, which promotes lesser-known destinations. Full design details will come with the launch.

**Why it matters:** Tourism is an employment-heavy services sector and a source of foreign exchange. The UN Tourism theme matches India's push for digital public infrastructure in the sector, including e-visa, the NIDHI+ registry and AI-based promotion.

**Key facts (as given in the backgrounder)**
- **Domestic tourist visits: 428.55 crore**; **international arrivals: 2.53 crore**; **foreign exchange earnings: ₹2,76,831 crore**.
- Tourism's share of GDP was **5.22% (2023-24)**, and the sector supports about **8.46 crore jobs**.
- **e-Visa** is available to nationals of **172 countries**. About **78%** of visas are now issued digitally.
- **Swadesh Darshan 2.0:** 53 projects worth ₹2,207.08 crore. **PRASHAD:** 54 pilgrimage projects worth ₹1,726.74 crore.
- **Cruise passengers** rose from **1.08 lakh to 4.62 lakh**, an increase of about 328%.
- World Tourism Day has been observed on 27 September since **1980** by **UN Tourism** (formerly UNWTO), marking the adoption of its Statutes in 1970.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (services, tourism); cross-tag GS1 Culture (heritage and pilgrimage circuits).

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (at the UN): India at the UN High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response — calls for an equitable PABS annex
articles.text:
At the UNGA-81 **High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response** in New York on **25 September 2026**, Union Health Secretary **Punya Salila Srivastava** described pandemic preparedness as a *shared responsibility*. She called the **WHO Pandemic Agreement (adopted May 2025)** a significant milestone, but said its credibility depends on a fair **Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS)** system.

**Why it matters:** This is the live fault line in global health governance. The PABS annex is still being negotiated, and until it is settled the Agreement cannot open for signature. India's position is typical of the Global South: countries that share pathogen samples and genetic data should be guaranteed access to the vaccines, diagnostics and therapeutics developed from them. It also stresses national sovereignty and flexibility in implementing **One Health**.

**Key facts**
- India cited its COVID-19 record: about **300 million vaccine doses to around 100 countries and two UN entities**, and medical supplies to **150+ countries**.
- India highlighted its whole-of-government, whole-of-society approach: expanding lab networks, emergency coordination, health-workforce capacity and diagnostics.
- The **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted by the **World Health Assembly in May 2025**. The **PABS annex** is being negotiated separately.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — International Relations (global health governance, WHO, UNGA); cross-tag GS2 Health.

articles.title: Deep depression 'Arnab' crosses the coast near Kalingapatnam — and the name never actually gets used — Geography
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Bay of Bengal system made landfall between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur, close to **Kalingapatnam (Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh)**, at about **02:47 IST on 24 September 2026**, and IMD kept it at **deep depression** intensity — so "Arnab", the Bangladesh-contributed name next in line, was never formally assigned.

**Exam angle (2–3 lines):** This is the cleanest "Places in News" + disaster-classification combination of the season. UPSC's favourite trap is exactly this gap — a named system versus an unnamed one — because a name is assigned only once a system reaches **cyclonic storm** intensity (≥62 kmph). Pair it with the withdrawal story: the **southwest monsoon withdrew from Delhi on 23 September 2026**, two days ahead of the normal 25 September date and the earliest exit since 2002.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Landfall ~02:47 IST, 24 Sep 2026, between **Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur**, near **Kalingapatnam**; gusts to **75 kmph**; intensity held ~12 hours post-landfall.
- Remained a **deep depression** (50–61 kmph), below the 62 kmph cyclonic-storm threshold — hence no name used. **"Arnab"** was contributed by **Bangladesh** (Bengali: "ocean").
- Red alert districts: **Koraput, Gajapati, Ganjam (Odisha)**; spillover rain into West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Telangana.
- Delhi monsoon withdrawal **23 Sep 2026** (normal: 25 Sep; earliest since **20 Sep 2002**); Safdarjung seasonal rain **728.6 mm** vs normal **629.7 mm** (+16%), still classed "normal".
- Withdrawal criteria applied: cessation of rainfall, falling lower-tropospheric moisture, and establishment of an **anticyclonic circulation**.

**Destination notebook:** GS1 — Geography (Climatology / Indian Monsoon) + GS3 — Disaster Management.

**Static anchor:** *NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography*, Ch. 10 "Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems" + *Shankar IAS / GC Leong* tropical cyclones. **Nudge:** on your cyclone page, write the full IMD intensity ladder (LPA → Depression 31–49 → Deep Depression 50–61 → Cyclonic Storm 62–87 → SCS 88–117 → VSCS 118–166 → ESCS 167–221 → Super Cyclone ≥222 kmph) and cross-link to the RSMC New Delhi naming note: 13-member WMO/ESCAP Panel, 169-name 2020 list, names never reused in the North Indian Ocean.

articles.title: The Crop Weather Watch Group puts satellite numbers on a drought in six states — Agriculture
articles.text:
**Headline:** At the **Crop Weather Watch Group** meeting of **21 September 2026** (reported 24 September), the **Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (NCFC)** flagged drought/soil-moisture stress across **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu**, with secondary stress in Punjab, Haryana, Kerala, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

**Exam angle:** This is the item to use when a question asks *how* India actually detects agricultural drought — the answer is a remote-sensing stack, not just rainfall departure. It also sets up the kharif-shortfall → rabi-risk chain as the monsoon retreats, and gives you a concrete case study for both the Manual for Drought Management and the "technology in agriculture" GS3 slot.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Analysis window **1 June – 19 September 2026**; dry spells of **two to three weeks** (days with <2.5 mm rain) in several states.
- Data stack: **IMD** rainfall + **SMAP** root-zone soil moisture + **VIIRS** NDVI/LSWI at **500 m** + **Sentinel-1 SAR** backscatter + **CWC** reservoir levels.
- **NDVI down more than 30%** in **Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Barmer (Rajasthan)** and **Kutch (Gujarat)**.
- Impact reported: delayed paddy transplanting, with some farmers shifting out of paddy.
- **NCFC**, New Delhi, sits under the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and runs **FASAL** and **NADAMS**.
- Companion Agriculture nugget for the same day: **Z.T. Lalrithangi** of **Sangau, Lawngtlai district, Mizoram** named among FAO's **"100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems"** (100 selected from 600+ nominees across 131 countries; 2 Indians), under the UN's **International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026**; award at the World Food Forum, Rome, 12–16 Oct 2026.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Agriculture (+ GS3 Disaster Management for the drought-declaration machinery).

**Static anchor:** *Mrunal* Agriculture pillar (irrigation, cropping patterns, drought) + *Shankar IAS* chapter on agriculture and climate. **Nudge:** add a one-page box to your drought notes distinguishing **meteorological / hydrological / agricultural** drought, and cross-link the **Manual for Drought Management (2016, revised 2020)** — mandatory indicator (rainfall deviation + dry spell) plus four impact-indicator classes, Trigger-1 and Trigger-2, declaration by the **State Government**, SDRF/NDRF assistance.

articles.title: Edible-oil duties cut again — crude sunflower oil goes to zero — Economy
articles.text:
**Headline:** **Notification No. 31/2026-Customs dated 23 September 2026** (Department of Revenue) cut basic customs duty across the edible-oil basket **with effect from 24 September 2026**, taking **crude sunflower oil to 0%**.

**Exam angle:** A textbook illustration of tariffs used as an anti-inflation instrument, and of the **crude-versus-refined duty differential** as industrial policy — the gap was widened, which favours importing crude and refining at home. The trade-off is the classic one UPSC likes: consumer price relief versus protection for domestic oilseed growers under NMEO.

**Facts to memorise:**
- **Crude palm and crude soybean oil: 10% → 5%.** **Crude sunflower oil: 10% → 0%.**
- **Refined palm and refined soybean oil: 32.5% → 27.5%.** **Refined sunflower oil: 32.5% → 22.5%.**
- Effective **24 Sep 2026**; industry directed to pass the benefit through ahead of the festive season.
- Trigger cited in reporting: **WPI-based food inflation at 7.1% in August 2026, a 20-month high**.
- Crude–refined gap widened (palm/soy: 22.5 pp; sunflower: 22.5 pp) — protects domestic refining capacity.
- India imports **over half** of its edible-oil requirement; **palm oil** is the single largest imported edible oil.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (External Sector / Inflation) with an Agriculture cross-entry.

**Static anchor:** *Mrunal* Economy pillar on inflation and on foreign trade/tariffs. **Nudge:** on your edible-oil page, tabulate **BCD + AIDC + Social Welfare Surcharge** as the three layers of an effective import duty, and cross-link **NMEO-Oil Palm (2021, ₹11,040 crore, North East and A&N focus)** and **NMEO-Oilseeds (₹10,103 crore, 2024-25 to 2030-31, under Krishonnati Yojana)** so the "protect the farmer vs cool the CPI" tension sits on one page.

articles.title: Ministry of Science & Technology (DBT / BIRAC): India's first commercial-scale bio-based biodegradable plastic facility launched under BioE3
articles.text:
A 100 TPA pilot-scale R&D facility for **Polylactic Acid (PLA) and co-polymers** was launched at Kumbhi, Uttar Pradesh, inside the complex of **Balrampur Chini Mills Limited (BCML)**. It converts sugar-based feedstock into compostable bioplastic, moving India from imported PLA towards indigenous biomanufacturing. This is the first commercial translation of the **BioE3 Policy** framework into a working plant.

**Why it matters:** PLA is the main drop-in substitute for single-use fossil plastics. Domestic PLA capacity links three policy goals at once — plastic-waste reduction under the EPR regime, "waste to wealth" use of sugar-industry by-products, and reduced import dependence in advanced materials.

**Key facts**
- Launched **24 September 2026**; supported by a **₹75 crore BIRAC grant**.
- Capacity: **100 tonnes per annum**, pilot/R&D scale.
- **BioE3** = *Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment* — the policy approved in 2024 to build high-performance biomanufacturing.
- India's **bioeconomy has grown from about US$10 billion (2014) to nearly US$195 billion**.
- Launched by **Dr. Jitendra Singh** (MoS, Science & Technology and Earth Sciences); present were Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale (Secretary, DBT and Chairman, BIRAC) and Dr. Dhananjay K. Tiwary (MD, BIRAC).

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Science & Technology (biotechnology, biomanufacturing); cross-tag GS3 Environment (plastic waste).

articles.title: Ministry of Defence (DRDO): First high-value deep-tech agreement under the TDF Scheme — an indigenous 20 millikelvin dilution refrigerator
articles.text:
DRDO signed its first high-value deep-technology agreement under the **Technology Development Fund (TDF)** with **Zero mK India Private Limited**, a Rajasthan-based start-up, to develop an indigenous **20 mK dilution refrigerator**. **Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL)**, a DRDO lab, provides technical mentorship and monitoring.

**Why it matters:** A dilution refrigerator is not a quantum computer but is the *enabling infrastructure* for superconducting qubit architectures — it holds hardware at a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero so fragile quantum states survive long enough to compute. India currently imports these systems, which is a strategic vulnerability when the end use is sensitive defence and cryptographic research. This is a direct industrial feed into the **National Quantum Mission**.

**Key facts**
- Agreement signed **24 September 2026**.
- **TDF corpus: ₹500 crore**; the scheme funds Indian industry, especially MSMEs and start-ups, to develop defence technologies, with DRDO as the implementing agency.
- Target: **20 millikelvin (0.02 K)** operating temperature.
- **Rajnath Singh** (Defence Minister) said the partnership would set a precedent for future DRDO–industry collaboration; Defence Secretary **Rajesh Kumar Singh** also spoke.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Science & Technology (quantum technology, indigenisation); cross-tag GS3 Internal Security (defence R&D ecosystem).

articles.title: Ministry of Culture: BRICS Theatre Festival 2026 announced — nine countries in New Delhi, 12–14 October
articles.text:
The Ministry of Culture will host the **BRICS Theatre Festival 2026** in New Delhi from **12 to 14 October 2026**, with the **National School of Drama (NSD) as nodal agency**. Theme: **"Shared Stories, Shared Futures."**

**Why it matters:** This is the cultural-diplomacy limb of **India's BRICS Presidency 2026** — the deliverable flowing from the **Bhopal Declaration** adopted at the BRICS Culture Ministers' Meeting in August 2026 and welcomed in the BRICS Leaders' Declaration. For GS2 it is a clean example of soft power institutionalised through a multilateral grouping; for GS1 it is an instance of state patronage of performing arts.

**Key facts**
- **Dates: 12–14 October 2026**; venues include the **National School of Drama, Kamani Auditorium, LTG Auditorium and Meghdoot Theatre**, New Delhi.
- **Nine BRICS member and partner countries**: India, Russia, South Africa, Iran, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Kazakhstan, Ethiopia.
- **Over 100 theatre practitioners, scholars and cultural representatives**; India presents two productions, Russia sends two theatre groups.
- Mandate covers **classical, contemporary and experimental** theatre plus workshops on performance traditions and stagecraft.
- **Vivek Aggarwal**, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, called it "an important cultural engagement under India's BRICS Presidency."

**Destination notebook:** GS1 — Art & Culture (performing arts, institutions); cross-tag GS2 IR (BRICS, cultural diplomacy).

---

### Also worth a line (24–25 September 2026)

- **Make in India completes 12 years (25 September).** The PM marked the anniversary of the 25 September 2014 launch, highlighting gains in manufacturing, investment and exports; DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce & Industry) is the nodal department. A PIB backgrounder has been issued — figures worth pulling directly from it when revising the manufacturing chapter.
- **Arogya Manthan 2026 inaugurated at Vigyan Bhawan (Health & Family Welfare),** marking **eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)**. *(PM-JAY's eight-year data was covered on 23 September; what is new here is the ABDM five-year milestone.)*
- **DDU-GKY 2.0 scaled up (Rural Development):** skill training for about **70,000 rural youth** from October 2026. *(UPDATE — the 19 September briefing carried 1,164 batches / 34,920 youth; the figure has roughly doubled.)*
- **Special Campaign 6.0 formally launched (DARPG),** with **e-waste and scrap management** as the headline focus. *(UPDATE — flagged as preparatory-phase on 23 September; the nationwide drive runs 2–31 October 2026.)*
- **ICAR-CMFRI advisory on tuna (Agriculture & Farmers Welfare):** consumers need not avoid tuna over parasite reports from the **Atlantic off Brazil**; fish examined along the Indian coast showed no external parasitic infestation. Director **Dr. Grinson George** stressed prompt evisceration during handling and that proper cooking kills parasites.
- **India–Netherlands water sector partnership (Jal Shakti)** advanced at the 9th India International Water Week 2026, alongside an **Indo-Africa WASH roundtable**.

articles.title: Planetary Health Check 2026: seven of nine planetary boundaries breached, and the food system is named as the dominant driver — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Planetary Health Check 2026, released on 21 September 2026 by the Planetary Boundaries Science Lab at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research and authored by 60-plus scientists, finds seven of the nine planetary boundaries transgressed and the trends worsening.

**Exam angle:** The **planetary boundaries** framework (Rockström and colleagues, 2009, out of the Stockholm Resilience Centre) is high-yield precisely because it is a *list with a structure* — nine processes, each with a quantified "safe operating space" — and UPSC likes lists whose membership can be tested. The exam-relevant news is not "things are bad"; it is (a) **which two remain within the safe space** — stratospheric ozone depletion and atmospheric aerosol loading — and (b) the report's new **food-system boundaries** framing, which argues that food production and consumption drive transgression across *all* nine. That last point is a genuinely quotable Mains line linking agriculture, land-use change, nitrogen–phosphorus flows and biodiversity in one causal chain.

**Memorise:**
- **Planetary Health Check 2026**, released **21 September 2026**; publisher: **Planetary Boundaries Science Lab, Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK)**; **60+ authors**
- **7 of 9** boundaries transgressed; the two still within the safe operating space: **stratospheric ozone depletion** and **atmospheric aerosol loading**
- The nine boundaries: climate change; biosphere integrity; land-system change; freshwater change; biogeochemical flows (N and P); ocean acidification; novel entities; stratospheric ozone depletion; atmospheric aerosol loading
- **Ocean acidification** was the most recent to be declared breached (2025 edition)
- Framework origin: **Rockström et al., 2009**, **Stockholm Resilience Centre**
- New in 2026: the first data-based **"food system boundaries"** framework — food named as the dominant driver of transgression

**Notebook:** GS3 — Environment (conservation, environmental pollution and degradation); GS1 for the ozone/aerosol physical-geography link.

**Static anchor:** *Shankar IAS Environment — "Planetary Boundaries" and the Ozone Depletion chapter.* **Update nudge:** write the nine boundaries as a single mnemonic line in the margin and tick the two safe ones; cross-link ozone depletion to the **Montreal Protocol / Kigali Amendment** page — the one boundary moving in the *right* direction is also the one with the strongest treaty behind it, and that contrast is the best available answer to "do environmental agreements work?"

articles.title: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: India showcases UHC, hepatitis elimination and sickle cell care at UNGA-81; joins the global OneSCD partnership
articles.text:
**Issuing body:** Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; India represented by Union Health Secretary **Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava**.

**What it is.** India took part in three global health engagements on the margins of the 81st UN General Assembly: the **7th Annual Ministerial Meeting of the Group of Friends of Universal Health Coverage and Global Health**; a side event on **"Advancing Global Action to Eliminate Hepatitis"**; and the launch of **OneSCD — a global partnership to advance equity and transform sickle cell care**.
